name: Citizenship by Descent

qualifying_event.description: A child acquires Estonian citizenship at birth if at least one parent is an Estonian citizen at the time of the child's birth, regardless of where the child is born. Separately, a child born in Estonia to stateless parents who have lawfully resided in Estonia for at least 5 years also acquires citizenship at birth.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Parent's proof of Estonian citizenship (passport or citizenship certificate) and the child's birth certificate showing the parental relationship.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires at least one parent to have been an Estonian citizen at the time of your birth, regardless of your country of birth.

evidence_required.document: Birth certificate establishing the parental relationship

sources.title: Ministry of the Interior of Estonia (siseministeerium.ee) -- Citizenship

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Estonia's initial build. This is genuine, unconditional jus sanguinis: citizenship passes through EITHER parent, at birth, with no registration deadline or generational cap mentioned on the source page -- a cleaner rule than several other countries in this dataset (contrast with Portugal's and Canada's recent generational-cap changes noted elsewhere in this project). dual_citizenship_allowed is deliberately left null: the source page states 'every citizen of Estonia also holds citizenship of the European Union' but does not address Estonia's policy on holding a non-EU second nationality, which multiple tier-3 sources describe as historically restricted with recent liberalisation -- not resolved to a confident answer with a tier-1 source in this pass. selection_method is 'automatic' since this is an at-birth entitlement, not an application assessed against discretion, which is also why status is 'published' despite citing only one source -- the fact pattern here is simple enough that one clear government statement was judged sufficient, unlike more contested figures elsewhere in this dataset.
